newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' profits up at start of 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' profits up at start of 1997.

text.p: U.S. manufacturing companies sold more and posted higher overall profits in the first quarter of this year than during the closing three months of 1996, the Commerce Department said on Monday.

A quarterly survey of about 8,300 companies showed that profits climbed in the first quarter to a seasonally adjusted 6.2 cents per dollar of sales from a revised 6 cents in the fourth quarter of last year.
Previously, the department said fourth-quarter profits had averaged 6.1 cents per sales dollar, but it revised that estimate downward modestly.

The first-quarter profits pickup occurred as the nation's gross domestic product, or GDP, accelerated to a booming 5.8 percent annual rate. Growth is expected to ease to less than half that rate in the current second quarter.

Manufacturers' profits after taxes during the first quarter totalled a seasonally adjusted $59.3 billion on net sales of $964.3 billion. In the fourth quarter, profits were a smaller $57.5 billion on net sales of $959.8 billion.

The pickup in first-quarter profits was concentrated among manufacturers of non-durable goods, including chemicals companies. In addition, petroleum producers and rubber, drug and paper companies all reported stronger profits, the department said.
As a group, non-durable goods producers reported that their profits rose to $31.2 billion in the first quarter from $29 billion in the fourth quarter, the department said.

By contrast, producers of longer-lasting and generally more-expensive durable goods reported that their profits after taxes fell to a seasonally adjusted $28.1 billion in the first quarter from $28.5 billion in the fourth quarter.
The department said that manufacturers of motor vehicles, fabricated metals, lumber, iron and steel, nonferrous metals and aircraft all had profit increases during the first quarter.
But producers of stone, clay and glass reported a loss during the first three months this year, partly because of unspecified non-recurring charges against first-quarter income.
In addition, manufacturers of machinery, furniture and fixtures said their profits were lower in the first quarter this year than at the end of last year, the department said.
